title: General inclusions for ideals generated by matrix minors
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring and $A$ a finite $p\times n$ matrix over $R$ [def-weil-matrix]. For $r\ge0$, let $J_r(A)$ be the ideal generated by the determinants [def-weil-pbc-matrix-determinant] of its $r\times r$ submatrices [def-weil-submatrix], with $J_0(A)=R$ and $J_r(A)=0$ when $r>\min(p,n)$. Then (1) $J_{r+1}(A)\subseteq J_r(A)$; (2) if $B$ is a $p\times(n+d)$ matrix whose first $n$ columns are $A$, where $d\ge0$, then $J_{r+d}(B)\subseteq J_r(A)$; (3) for every $n\times n$ matrix $C$ over $R$, one has $J_r(AC)\subseteq J_r(A)$, where $(AC)_{ij}=\sum_{h=1}^n A_{ih}C_{hj}$. These statements include empty matrices and $r=0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07Z7 (lemma-ideals-generated-by-minors), parts (1), (2), (3); (2) and (3) written for transposed matrices so that appended rows become appended columns and left multiplication becomes right multiplication.

proof.text: For an ideal generated by a set of determinants, it suffices to put each generating determinant in the proposed target ideal: that ideal is closed under sums and multiplication by ring elements. When $r=0$, all three conclusions hold since their target is $J_0(A)=R$. Hence assume $r\ge1$. Whenever a source ideal has no minors of the indicated size it is zero, so its asserted inclusion is automatic. This treats empty row sets, empty column sets, and all oversized-minor cases without choosing nonexistent indices.

source.place: Tag 07Z7 (lemma-ideals-generated-by-minors), conventions and reduction to generators

proof.text: For (1), take an $(r+1)$-minor $Q$ of $A$. Apply [lem-trf-minor-laplace-coefficient-formula] with $q=r+1$, $s=r$ and $T=\{1,\ldots,r\}$. Each $Q_{I,T}$ is an $r$-minor of $A$; its coefficient is the signed complementary $1$-minor, hence an element of $R$. The identity expresses $\det Q$ as a finite sum of elements of $J_r(A)$. Step 1 gives the inclusion. The formula includes the signs from the cofactor expansion, with no invertibility hypothesis.

For (2), for each $(r+d)$-minor $B_{I,J}$ apply [lem-trf-column-extension-minor-coefficients] to $B$ and its first $n$ columns $A$. Its displayed evaluation identity writes this determinant as a sum of coefficients in $R$ times $r$-minors of $A$. Every summand lies in $J_r(A)$, and Step 1 gives $J_{r+d}(B)\subseteq J_r(A)$. At $d=0$ the coefficients are Kronecker deltas, so this is equality; no minors are selected when their index sets do not exist.

source.place: Tag 07Z7 (lemma-ideals-generated-by-minors)(2), transposed form, induction by expansion in the last added column

proof.text: For (3), choose row and column sets $I\subseteq\{1,\ldots,p\}$ and $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$ with $|I|=|J|=r$, both ordered increasingly. Let $A_I$ be the $r\times n$ matrix formed by those rows of $A$, and $C_J$ the $n\times r$ matrix formed by those columns of $C$. Entrywise, the chosen submatrix of $AC$ is $A_I C_J$, because both entries are $\sum_{h=1}^n A_{i,h}C_{h,j}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-cauchy-binet] with its $m=r$, its $n=n$, and matrices $A_I,C_J$. It gives $$\det((AC)_{I,J})=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\},\ |S|=r}\det(A_{I,S})\det(C_{S,J}).$$ Every first determinant is an $r$-minor of $A$ and hence belongs to $J_r(A)$; every second determinant is an element of $R$. Therefore the displayed sum belongs to $J_r(A)$. Taking the generated ideal proves $J_r(AC)\subseteq J_r(A)$. If $r>\min(p,n)$, both source and target have no such minors and are zero, as already treated in Step 1.

mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q81-5ef7e909a (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the re-split repair note for this item (released 2026-10-22; live and side-live copies are identical). The live item is still at the base, so no other group has superseded it. I read the source, Stacks 07Z7 in more-algebra.tex at line 1326. The item statement is the transposed form and is unchanged.

Old step 2 (column cofactor expansion via the adjugate node) is now the new node lem-trf-minor-laplace-coefficient-formula. That node is the general Laplace expansion along any s-column set T. I checked the sign by hand: at q=2 it gives ad-cb for T={1} and da-bc for T={2}. For s=0, s=q and q=0 it reduces to 1=1. In the parent's case (q=r+1, s=r, T={1..r}) the sign works out to (-1)^(a+q), which is ordinary expansion along the last column. Only that single-column case is actually used. That case is already in Mathlib (det_succ_column) and in the DAG (the adjugate node), so the node is more general than needed. I accept this because the node is true and comparable in size to the other new node; it is a note for the maintainer, not a fault.

Old step 3 (induction on the number of added columns) is now lem-trf-column-extension-minor-coefficients. The coefficients are explicit integer polynomials L_d defined by a recursion that expands along the last selected column j_q. All remaining columns are at most n+d-1, so they lie in the shorter matrix, and the sign (-1)^(a+q) matches the cofactor expansion. I checked the cases d=0; r=0, d=1; r=1, d=1 with the minor containing or omitting the new column; vacuous selections; and the zero ring. The node gives an explicit identity rather than restating clause (2). The recursion is defining data, not a proof sketch, so it is not a B1 fault. The node does not depend on the Laplace node, so the two can be worked on in parallel.

Steps 1 and 4 are kept word for word. I checked step 4's use of Cauchy-Binet against that node's statement: m=r, and the chosen submatrix of AC equals A_I C_J entry by entry. The retained Cauchy-Binet tool_uses entry is accepted. The parent proof is 2319 characters of assembly. Its proof_deps are exactly the three cited nodes, and there is no cycle.

I found no duplicates: rg -L for laplace, cofactor and complementary minors over the snapshot DAG finds only unrelated nodes. Mathlib has single-column expansions only. Both new nodes meet B1-B7: statement only, self-contained, the matrix/submatrix/determinant definitions cited, the 07Z7 hint as source, and correct blueprint.from/via. I could not check the recorded searches against the search log, which exists only on the Codex machine. No SGA is cited. No fixes were made.

lean.statement: theorem minorIdeal_inclusions {R : Type u} [CommRing R] (p n r d : ℕ) (A : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin n) R) : minorIdeal p n (r + 1) A ≤ minorIdeal p n r A ∧ (∀ (B : Matrix (Fin p) (Fin (n + d)) R), (∀ (i : Fin p) (j : Fin n), B i (Fin.castAdd d j) = A i j) → minorIdeal p (n + d) (r + d) B ≤ minorIdeal p n r A) ∧ (∀ (C : Matrix (Fin n) (Fin n) R), minorIdeal p n r (A * C) ≤ minorIdeal p n r A)
